text.p: Medical instrument designer Polartechnics Ltd said on Thursday it plans to form an alliance with Ethicon Inc, a unit of Johnson & Johnson for the commercialisation of its cancer detection device Polarprobe.
Polartechnics said the sales and marketing agreement for its cervical cancer and precancer detection device would provide Ethicon with an exclusive licence in most parts of the world.
It said it would retain rights to the product in Australasia, Taiwan, South Korea, Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia, and Indochina.
The company said Ethicon would pay Polartechnics a total of up to US$18 million as part of the agreement, to be triggered by completion of certain milestones which it did not specify.
Polartechnics chairman Tony Grey said the company would remain responsible for the manufacture and R&D operations of the Polarprobe device.
It said the two companies would work together to obtain regulatory approvals ahead of marketing, including in the United States and Europe.
Polartechnics would continue to fund all clinical trials.
The company's shares, which had been suspended or subject to a trading halt for three days prior to the announcement, were 82 cents higher at A$3.30 at 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT).
